# CVE-2026-135720 — FFmpeg: NULL pointer dereference in DASH LCEVC grouping

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135720 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/dashdec.c::dash_read_header` |
| **Affected** | 9.0 before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`fba9c09`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference) |
| **Impact** | When building LCEVC stream groups, `dash_read_header()` selected representations that had a dependency ID and associated streams but no `codecs` string. The builder dereferenced the missing codecs, crashing the demuxer. An attacker could supply a crafted MPD manifest to trigger it |
| **Vector** | attacker-supplied DASH MPD manifest |
| **Trigger** | representation with `dependencyid` and associated streams but no `codecs` |

The vulnerable selection:

```c
// dashdec.c — pre-fix (verbatim in the lab)
if (!rep->dependencyid || !rep->nb_assoc_stream)
    continue;
// ... LCEVC group builder uses rep->codecs -> NULL deref
```

The fix adds the missing check:

```c
// fixed (commit fba9c09, verbatim in the lab)
if (!rep->dependencyid || !rep->codecs || !rep->nb_assoc_stream)
    continue;
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The selection predicate for LCEVC grouping required a dependency ID and
associated streams but omitted the `codecs` field. A crafted manifest could
satisfy the first two while leaving `codecs` NULL, and the group builder
dereferenced it. The fix adds `!rep->codecs` to the skip condition.

## 2. Reproduction environment

| service | image | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dash-vuln` | `cve-2026-135720:vuln` | unchecked codecs, ASan+UBSan |
| `dash-fixed` | `cve-2026-135720:fixed` | verbatim NULL check |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-135720-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

The C harness uses the selection guard from both commits with a crafted
representation that has a dependency ID and associated streams but no codecs.

## 3. Running the environment

```sh

./run-lab.sh up        # cve135720lab network: dash-vuln / dash-fixed
./run-lab.sh sweep
./run-lab.sh down
```

| **Impact** | Stream language metadata was written unescaped into the `xml:lang` attribute of a generated TTML document. An attacker supplying media with a crafted Language value — for example a Matroska subtitle track — could inject XML markup and alter downstream parsing or rendering |
| **Vector** | attacker-supplied media with crafted Language metadata converted to TTML |
| **Trigger** | Language value containing `"`, `<`, `>` such as `en"><injected .../>x="` |

The vulnerable write:

```c
// ttmlenc.c — pre-fix (verbatim in the lab)
const char *printed_lang = (lang && lang->value) ? lang->value : "";
...
avio_printf(pb, " xml:lang=\"%s\"", printed_lang);   // raw value
```

The fix escapes the value:

```c
// fixed (commit bcb5d56, verbatim logic in the lab)
ret = av_escape(&printed_lang, lang ? lang->value : "", NULL,
                AV_ESCAPE_MODE_XML, 0);
if (ret < 0) return ret;
...
avio_printf(pb, " xml:lang=\"%s\"", printed_lang);   // escaped
```

---

## 1. Root cause

Metadata values are attacker-controlled data, but the language tag was
interpolated directly into an XML attribute. Quotes and angle brackets in the
value therefore became part of the document structure. The fix escapes the
value with `av_escape()` in XML mode before interpolation.

# CVE-2026-135708 — FFmpeg: arbitrary file destruction through WHIP `Location` scheme

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135708 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/whip.c::exchange_sdp` |
| **Affected** | 8.0 before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`96994cb`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-20 (Improper Input Validation) |
| **Impact** | A malicious WHIP server could return a `file:` URL in the `Location` header. The muxer stored it as the session resource URL, and `dispose_session()` later opened it read-write with truncation, destroying arbitrary user-writable files. Other schemes could redirect requests to unintended protocols |
| **Vector** | malicious WHIP server responding to an SDP exchange |
| **Trigger** | `Location: file:///tmp/whip-victim` |

The vulnerable handling:

```c
// whip.c — pre-fix (verbatim in the lab)
if (ff_http_get_new_location(whip_uc)) {
    whip->whip_resource_url = av_strdup(ff_http_get_new_location(whip_uc));
    ...
}
// dispose_session() later opens whip_resource_url with O_TRUNC
```

The fix validates the protocol:

```c
// fixed (commit 96994cb, verbatim in the lab)
proto_name = avio_find_protocol_name(ff_http_get_new_location(whip_uc));
if (!proto_name || !av_strstart(proto_name, "http", NULL)) {
    av_log(whip, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Unsupported resource url %s\n", ...);
    ret = AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;
    goto end;
}
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The `Location` header from a server was trusted as a resource URL without
validating its scheme. Because teardown opens that URL read-write with
truncation, a `file:` scheme turned a protocol redirect into a destructive file
write. The fix restricts the resource URL to `http*` protocols.

## 2. Reproduction environment

| service | image | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `whip-vuln` | `cve-2026-135708:vuln` | unchecked scheme |
| `whip-fixed` | `cve-2026-135708:fixed` | verbatim scheme guard |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-135708-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

The C harness uses the scheme check from both commits with a `file:` Location.
It seeds a victim file, runs teardown, and reports whether the file was
truncated — a real, observable file-destruction primitive.

# CVE-2026-135715 — FFmpeg: NULL pointer dereference in the AVIF muxer

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135715 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/movenc.c::mov_init` (AVIF muxer) |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`6fdfafa`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference) |
| **Impact** | When an AVIF output contained a second (alpha) stream with an unknown pixel format, `av_pix_fmt_desc_get()` returned NULL and `pixdesc->nb_components` dereferenced it, crashing the application. A primary stream with an unknown format was similarly unchecked |
| **Vector** | attacker-controlled input encoded to AVIF with an alpha stream |
| **Trigger** | AVIF output whose alpha stream has an unknown pixel format |

The vulnerable check:

```c
// movenc.c — pre-fix (behavior in the lab)
const AVPixFmtDescriptor *pixdesc =
    av_pix_fmt_desc_get(s->streams[1]->codecpar->format);
if (pixdesc->nb_components != 1) { ... }   // pixdesc may be NULL
```

The fix validates both descriptors:

```c
// fixed (commit 6fdfafa, verbatim in the lab)
if (!av_pix_fmt_desc_get(s->streams[0]->codecpar->format)) {
    av_log(s, AV_LOG_ERROR, "AVIF output requires a known pixel format\n");
    return AVERROR(EINVAL);
}
...
if (!pixdesc || pixdesc->nb_components != 1) {
    av_log(s, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Second stream for AVIF (alpha) output must have exactly one plane\n");
    return AVERROR(EINVAL);
}
```

---

## 1. Root cause

`av_pix_fmt_desc_get()` returns NULL for unknown or invalid pixel formats. The
muxer assumed a descriptor always existed and dereferenced it without a NULL
check. The fix checks the descriptor for both the primary and alpha streams
before reading `nb_components`.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `avif-vuln` | `cve-2026-135715:vuln` | unchecked descriptor, ASan+UBSan |
| `avif-fixed` | `cve-2026-135715:fixed` | verbatim NULL guards |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-135715-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

The C harness uses the guards from both commits with an alpha stream whose
pixel format makes `av_pix_fmt_desc_get()` return NULL.

# CVE-2026-135713 — FFmpeg: NULL pointer dereference in `mms_open()`

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135713 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/mmst.c::mms_open` |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`94c3187`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference) |
| **Impact** | When a malicious MMS server sent an ASF header lacking a packet size or stream properties, `mms_open()` jumped to its failure label with the error variable still zero. The state was freed and `mms_open()` returned success; the client's first read then dereferenced the freed/NULL state, crashing it |
| **Vector** | malicious MMS server responding to an MMST connection |
| **Trigger** | ASF header with no packet size or stream count |

The vulnerable failure path:

```c
// mmst.c — pre-fix (verbatim in the lab)
if (!mms->asf_packet_len || !mms->stream_num)
    goto fail;                 // err is still 0 here
...
fail:
    mms_close(h);              // frees state
    return err;                // returns 0 = success
```

The fix sets an error before failing:

```c
// fixed (commit 94c3187, verbatim in the lab)
if (!mms->asf_packet_len || !mms->stream_num) {
    err = AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;
    goto fail;
}
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The failure label returned a shared `err` variable. On the earlier success path
`err` was zero, and the malformed-header check jumped to `fail` without
assigning a new error. The function therefore freed its state and reported
success. The fix assigns `AVERROR_INVALIDDATA` so the caller stops before using
the invalid state.

## 2. Reproduction environment

| service | image | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mms-vuln` | `cve-2026-135713:vuln` | unchecked error assignment, ASan+UBSan |
| `mms-fixed` | `cve-2026-135713:fixed` | verbatim error assignment |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-135713-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

The C harness reproduces the error handling from both commits with a malformed
header (`asf_packet_len=0`, `stream_num=0`) and a caller that reads on success.

# CVE-2026-135718 — FFmpeg: out-of-bounds read in DVD menu audio stream handling

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135718 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/dvdvideodec.c::dvdvideo_ifo_open` / `dvdvideo_audio_stream_add_all` |
| **Affected** | 7.0 before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`cc7f5bc`** — AISLE-2026-0111-00216 |
| **CWE** | CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read) |
| **Impact** | The title path rejected more than 8 audio streams, but the menu path did not. A crafted DVD image whose menu IFO declared more than 8 audio streams made `dvdvideo_audio_stream_add_all()` read past the fixed 8-entry `audio_control` array, crashing the demuxer |
| **Vector** | attacker-supplied crafted DVD image |
| **Trigger** | menu IFO declaring 9 audio streams |

The vulnerable path:

```c
// dvdvideodec.c — pre-fix (behavior in the lab)
// menu path: no check that nr_of_vmgm_audio_streams <= 8
for (int i = 0; i < nb_streams; i++)
    ... c->play_state.pgc->audio_control[i] ...   // 8-entry array
```

The fix validates the menu count at IFO open:

```c
// fixed (commit cc7f5bc, verbatim in the lab)
if ((!c->opt_menu_vts && c->vmg_ifo->vmgi_mat->nr_of_vmgm_audio_streams > 8) ||
    ( c->opt_menu_vts && c->vts_ifo->vtsi_mat->nr_of_vtsm_audio_streams > 8)) {
    av_log(s, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Menu has invalid headers (too many audio streams)\n");
    return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;
}
```

---

## 1. Root cause

Two code paths consumed the same fixed-size `audio_control` array. Only one
validated the stream count from the IFO metadata. Because the count is
attacker-controlled, the unvalidated menu path could index past the array. The
fix applies the same upper-bound check to both paths.

## 2. Reproduction environment

| service | image | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dvd-vuln` | `cve-2026-135718:vuln` | unchecked menu count, ASan+UBSan |
| `dvd-fixed` | `cve-2026-135718:fixed` | verbatim count guard |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-135718-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

The C harness uses the guard from both commits with a menu IFO declaring 9
audio streams against an 8-entry `audio_control` array.

# CVE-2026-135706 — FFmpeg: heap buffer overflow in `modplug_read_header()`

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135706 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/libmodplug.c::modplug_read_header` |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`edc96a2`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-122 (Heap Buffer Overflow) |
| **Impact** | The module input buffer was allocated with `max_size` instead of the actual number of bytes to read (`sz`). When a crafted module file left `max_size` at zero, `avio_read()` wrote `sz` bytes into a zero-byte allocation, corrupting the heap |
| **Vector** | attacker-supplied module file passed to the libmodplug demuxer |
| **Trigger** | a module file that yields `max_size=0` with a nonzero read size |

The vulnerable allocation:

```c
// libmodplug.c — pre-fix (verbatim in the lab)
modplug->buf = av_malloc(modplug->max_size);   // may be 0
...
sz = avio_read(pb, modplug->buf, sz);          // writes sz bytes
```

The fix allocates the bytes actually read:

```c
// fixed (commit edc96a2, verbatim in the lab)
modplug->buf = av_malloc(sz);
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The allocation size and the read size came from different fields. `max_size` is
metadata that an attacker can leave unset, while `sz` is the number of bytes
`avio_read()` will actually write. Allocating the former and writing the latter
produces a heap overflow whenever `max_size < sz`. The fix uses `sz` for the
allocation.

## 2. Reproduction environment

| service | image | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mp-vuln` | `cve-2026-135706:vuln` | undersized allocation, ASan+UBSan |
| `mp-fixed` | `cve-2026-135706:fixed` | verbatim `sz` allocation |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-135706-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

The C harness uses the allocation line from both commits with `sz=32` and
`max_size=0`; a volatile sink prevents the write from being optimized away.

# mishe-tauftauf2shell — runtime2shell impact and RCE research plant

This repository is a Mishe plant with two general goals: **reaching rung 4
(demonstrated security impact) and, where a measured path exists, rung 5
(working remote command execution) for memory-safety vulnerabilities in
language runtimes and web-facing servers — the "X2Shell" family** — starting
with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) and Ruby2Shell
(CVE-2026-132825), and extending to similar classes the operator admits
under its standing mandate. Rung 5 is additive and per-build, never a reason
to relabel a pointer fault or harness-only marker as RCE. Everything here is
CC0. The durable products are the reproducible technical reports under
`reports/`; the laboratory under `lab/` is the means.

## Roles

- **one mind per target** (`ruby2shell`, `php2shell`, `node2shell`, and
  every target the operator admits) — each carries its own investigation:
  builds affected and patched runtimes, writes harnesses, instruments
  processes, runs debuggers, drives toward rung 4 and, where a measured
  path exists, rung 5 stage by stage, authors its report.
- **witness** — the independent verifier. Fresh context: re-runs claimed
  reproductions, hunts counterexamples, enforces the evidence ladder. The
  author's report is never acceptance.
- **operator** — the human owner's standing delegate with an expanded
  mandate: besides approving scoped work in place of the person, it holds
  the owner's standing approvals (recorded in the site's
  `operator/standing-approvals.md`) and actively **looks for similar
  things** — new X2Shell-class public claims, advisories and research
  worth a rung-4 or rung-5 attempt — proposing new targets with evidence,
  without asking each time. It is a mind, not a person; it never approves changes
  to this charter, systemd units or engine configuration, access to other
  plants or nodes, host-guard or credential changes, or anything off
  loopback.

One wake per role at a time; up to the site's `wake-concurrency.json` run
at once. Only the `omp` engine wakes minds here. No `claude`, no `codex`.

## Working in Mishe

A mind is a persistent identity (wall, intentions, history), not a
persistent process. You are woken for one turn by a trigger — an addressed
message, a changed signal, a due intention — and handed a dossier. Start
from it; the short `mishe` command resolves this site from
`$MISHE_SEED_HOME`, and an explicit `--home SITE_HOME` overrides it.
Resolve site-home paths to the absolute path before passing them to tools.

Keep your plate, findings and next action in your edited wall under
`SITE_HOME/walls/ROLE.md`, written for a human who has nothing else open:
what you are working on and why, the exact next command or edit, short
quoted evidence with where to look, and what would change your mind.
Update it while you work, not only at yield. Ask peers through addressed
messages on the shared chat tape. DMs are visible, not private.

Commit your own scoped work on the single `main` branch; a completed
checked change is committed, not parked. End every wake with
`mishe yield --result changed|verified|blocked`, your updated wall on
stdin; `--continue`, `--again DURATION` and `--when signal:NAME=VALUE`
schedule follow-up. A wake that ends without a yield is an unknown effect;
the next wake reconciles it first. While research is active, keep the chain
back-to-back: `--again 300`, never longer than the pin's cap; a genuine
wait for evidence is a `--when signal:` condition, not a long timer.

## Evidence discipline

Every finding carries evidence: the exact build, the exact input, the
observed bytes, and where they live. Distinguish, and never collapse:

1. **suspected vulnerability** — reasoning from source or claims, no trigger;
2. **reproducible crash** — a deterministic input that faults the lab process;
3. **confirmed memory corruption** — observed memory state proving
   corruption (ASan/UBSan/Valgrind report, debugger inspection), not just
   a crash;
4. **demonstrated security impact** — control exercised in the lab build
   (chosen bytes at chosen offsets; pointer control; benign marker
   execution), honestly labeled with the conditions it needed;
5. **working remote command execution** — attacker-controlled wire or
   request input makes a live target process on loopback execute a
   lab-chosen benign command, with an observed side effect and vulnerable,
   fixed and safe-input controls. Record the exact build, configuration,
   authentication, ASLR, grooming and triggering conditions; independent
   witness replay is required for ESTABLISHED. In-process harness markers,
   synthetic consumers and debugger-forced execution remain rung-4
   mechanics, not rung 5.

# mishe-tauftauf2shell — runtime2shell impact and RCE research plant

This repository is a Mishe plant with two general goals: **reaching rung 4
(demonstrated security impact) and, where a measured path exists, rung 5
(working remote command execution) for memory-safety vulnerabilities in
language runtimes and web-facing servers — the "X2Shell" family** — starting
with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) and Ruby2Shell
(CVE-2026-132825), and extending to similar classes the operator admits
under its standing mandate. Rung 5 is additive and per-build, never a reason
to relabel a pointer fault or harness-only marker as RCE. Everything here is
CC0. The durable products are the reproducible technical reports under
`reports/`; the laboratory under `lab/` is the means.

## Roles

- **one mind per target** (`ruby2shell`, `php2shell`, `node2shell`, and
  every target the operator admits) — each carries its own investigation:
  builds affected and patched runtimes, writes harnesses, instruments
  processes, runs debuggers, drives toward rung 4 and, where a measured
  path exists, rung 5 stage by stage, authors its report.
- **witness** — the independent verifier. Fresh context: re-runs claimed
  reproductions, hunts counterexamples, enforces the evidence ladder. The
  author's report is never acceptance.
- **operator** — the human owner's standing delegate with an expanded
  mandate: besides approving scoped work in place of the person, it holds
  the owner's standing approvals (recorded in the site's
  `operator/standing-approvals.md`) and actively **looks for similar
  things** — new X2Shell-class public claims, advisories and research
  worth a rung-4 or rung-5 attempt — proposing new targets with evidence,
  without asking each time. It is a mind, not a person; it never approves changes
  to this charter, systemd units or engine configuration, access to other
  plants or nodes, host-guard or credential changes, or anything off
  loopback.

One wake per role at a time; up to the site's `wake-concurrency.json` run
at once. Only the `omp` engine wakes minds here. No `claude`, no `codex`.

## Working in Mishe

A mind is a persistent identity (wall, intentions, history), not a
persistent process. You are woken for one turn by a trigger — an addressed
message, a changed signal, a due intention — and handed a dossier. Start
from it; the short `mishe` command resolves this site from
`$MISHE_SEED_HOME`, and an explicit `--home SITE_HOME` overrides it.
Resolve site-home paths to the absolute path before passing them to tools.

Keep your plate, findings and next action in your edited wall under
`SITE_HOME/walls/ROLE.md`, written for a human who has nothing else open:
what you are working on and why, the exact next command or edit, short
quoted evidence with where to look, and what would change your mind.
Update it while you work, not only at yield. Ask peers through addressed
messages on the shared chat tape. DMs are visible, not private.

Commit your own scoped work on the single `main` branch; a completed
checked change is committed, not parked. End every wake with
`mishe yield --result changed|verified|blocked`, your updated wall on
stdin; `--continue`, `--again DURATION` and `--when signal:NAME=VALUE`
schedule follow-up. A wake that ends without a yield is an unknown effect;
the next wake reconciles it first. While research is active, keep the chain
back-to-back: `--again 300`, never longer than the pin's cap; a genuine
wait for evidence is a `--when signal:` condition, not a long timer.

## Evidence discipline

Every finding carries evidence: the exact build, the exact input, the
observed bytes, and where they live. Distinguish, and never collapse:

1. **suspected vulnerability** — reasoning from source or claims, no trigger;
2. **reproducible crash** — a deterministic input that faults the lab process;
3. **confirmed memory corruption** — observed memory state proving
   corruption (ASan/UBSan/Valgrind report, debugger inspection), not just
   a crash;
4. **demonstrated security impact** — control exercised in the lab build
   (chosen bytes at chosen offsets; pointer control; benign marker
   execution), honestly labeled with the conditions it needed;
5. **working remote command execution** — attacker-controlled wire or
   request input makes a live target process on loopback execute a
   lab-chosen benign command, with an observed side effect and vulnerable,
   fixed and safe-input controls. Record the exact build, configuration,
   authentication, ASLR, grooming and triggering conditions; independent
   witness replay is required for ESTABLISHED. In-process harness markers,
   synthetic consumers and debugger-forced execution remain rung-4
   mechanics, not rung 5.

Unknowns stay UNKNOWN. Missing, failed or expired observations are never

# CVE-2026-135705 — FFmpeg: out-of-bounds read in `ff_h264_parse_framesize()`

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135705 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/rtpdec_h264.c::ff_h264_parse_framesize` |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`e5fe2cb`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read) |
| **Impact** | When parsing an SDP `a=framesize` attribute that lacks a height, `atoi(p + 1)` read past the line buffer. An attacker controlling an RTSP DESCRIBE response or a crafted `.sdp` file could crash clients or cause parsing of stale stack bytes |
| **Vector** | attacker-controlled RTSP DESCRIBE response or SDP file |
| **Trigger** | `a=framesize:96 320` (no `-height` suffix) |

The vulnerable parse:

```c
// rtpdec_h264.c — pre-fix (verbatim in the lab)
while (*p && *p != '-' && (dst - buf1) < sizeof(buf1) - 1)
    *dst++ = *p++;
*dst = '\0';
par->width  = atoi(buf1);
par->height = atoi(p + 1);   // p points at NUL when no '-' -> OOB read
```

The fix rejects malformed attributes:

```c
// fixed (commit e5fe2cb, verbatim in the lab)
*dst = '\0';
if (*p != '-')
    return;
par->width  = atoi(buf1);
par->height = atoi(p + 1);
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The copy loop terminates on a `-`, on the end of the string, or when the fixed
`buf1` fills. The code assumed a `-` was always present and unconditionally
parsed `p + 1` as the height. With a framesize attribute lacking a separator,
`p` points at the terminating NUL and `p + 1` is outside the line buffer. The
fix returns early when no separator was found.

## 2. Reproduction environment

| service | image | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `h264-vuln` | `cve-2026-135705:vuln` | pre-fix parse, ASan+UBSan |
| `h264-fixed` | `cve-2026-135705:fixed` | verbatim separator guard |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-135705-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

The C harness uses the exact `ff_h264_parse_framesize()` from both commits with
an exactly sized heap buffer holding `framesize:96 320`, so the one-byte-over
read lands in ASan's redzone.

# CVE-2026-135703 — FFmpeg: uninitialized heap leak in ASF RTP reassembly

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135703 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/rtpdec_asf.c::asfrtp_parse_packet` |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`f7fa69e`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-908 (Use of Uninitialized Resource) |
| **Impact** | The packet-length check only rejected a negative `FFMIN(cur_len, len-off)`. An oversized declared length passed, grew the reassembly buffer, but copied only the clamped number of bytes — leaving a gap of uninitialized heap that was emitted to the caller. A malicious RTSP server could leak heap contents |
| **Vector** | malicious RTSP server with an `x-asf-pf` payload |
| **Trigger** | declared packet length greater than remaining bytes |

The vulnerable check:

```c
// rtpdec_asf.c — pre-fix (behavior in the lab)
if (FFMIN(cur_len, len - off) < 0) return -1;   // misses oversized cur_len
out_len += cur_len;                              // grows by full (oversized) value
av_reallocp(&asf->buf, out_len);
memcpy(asf->buf + prev_len, buf + off, FFMIN(cur_len, len - off));   // copies less
```

The fix rejects out-of-range lengths:

```c
// fixed (commit f7fa69e, verbatim in the lab)
if (cur_len < 0 || cur_len > len - off) return -1;
...
memcpy(asf->buf + prev_len, buf + off, cur_len);
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The validation used the clamped value while the allocation used the unclamped
one, so the buffer was larger than the data written into it. The fix validates
the true length before allocation, keeping allocation and copy in sync.

| `poc` | `cve-2026-135703-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

The Python harness uses the check from both commits with `cur_len=100000` and
only 50 bytes remaining.

# mishe-tauftauf2shell — runtime2shell impact and RCE research plant

This repository is a Mishe plant with two general goals: **reaching rung 4
(demonstrated security impact) and, where a measured path exists, rung 5
(working remote command execution) for memory-safety vulnerabilities in
language runtimes and web-facing servers — the "X2Shell" family** — starting
with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) and Ruby2Shell
(CVE-2026-132825), and extending to similar classes the operator admits
under its standing mandate. Rung 5 is additive and per-build, never a reason
to relabel a pointer fault or harness-only marker as RCE. Everything here is
CC0. The durable products are the reproducible technical reports under
`reports/`; the laboratory under `lab/` is the means.

## Roles

- **one mind per target** (`ruby2shell`, `php2shell`, `node2shell`, and
  every target the operator admits) — each carries its own investigation:
  builds affected and patched runtimes, writes harnesses, instruments
  processes, runs debuggers, drives toward rung 4 and, where a measured
  path exists, rung 5 stage by stage, authors its report.
- **witness** — the independent verifier. Fresh context: re-runs claimed
  reproductions, hunts counterexamples, enforces the evidence ladder. The
  author's report is never acceptance.
- **operator** — the human owner's standing delegate with an expanded
  mandate: besides approving scoped work in place of the person, it holds
  the owner's standing approvals (recorded in the site's
  `operator/standing-approvals.md`) and actively **looks for similar
  things** — new X2Shell-class public claims, advisories and research
  worth a rung-4 or rung-5 attempt — proposing new targets with evidence,
  without asking each time. It is a mind, not a person; it never approves changes
  to this charter, systemd units or engine configuration, access to other
  plants or nodes, host-guard or credential changes, or anything off
  loopback.

One wake per role at a time; up to the site's `wake-concurrency.json` run
at once. Only the `omp` engine wakes minds here. No `claude`, no `codex`.

## Working in Mishe

A mind is a persistent identity (wall, intentions, history), not a
persistent process. You are woken for one turn by a trigger — an addressed
message, a changed signal, a due intention — and handed a dossier. Start
from it; the short `mishe` command resolves this site from
`$MISHE_SEED_HOME`, and an explicit `--home SITE_HOME` overrides it.
Resolve site-home paths to the absolute path before passing them to tools.

Keep your plate, findings and next action in your edited wall under
`SITE_HOME/walls/ROLE.md`, written for a human who has nothing else open:
what you are working on and why, the exact next command or edit, short
quoted evidence with where to look, and what would change your mind.
Update it while you work, not only at yield. Ask peers through addressed
messages on the shared chat tape. DMs are visible, not private.

Commit your own scoped work on the single `main` branch; a completed
checked change is committed, not parked. End every wake with
`mishe yield --result changed|verified|blocked`, your updated wall on
stdin; `--continue`, `--again DURATION` and `--when signal:NAME=VALUE`
schedule follow-up. A wake that ends without a yield is an unknown effect;
the next wake reconciles it first. While research is active, keep the chain
back-to-back: `--again 300`, never longer than the pin's cap; a genuine
wait for evidence is a `--when signal:` condition, not a long timer.

## Evidence discipline

Every finding carries evidence: the exact build, the exact input, the
observed bytes, and where they live. Distinguish, and never collapse:

1. **suspected vulnerability** — reasoning from source or claims, no trigger;
2. **reproducible crash** — a deterministic input that faults the lab process;
3. **confirmed memory corruption** — observed memory state proving
   corruption (ASan/UBSan/Valgrind report, debugger inspection), not just
   a crash;
4. **demonstrated security impact** — control exercised in the lab build
   (chosen bytes at chosen offsets; pointer control; benign marker
   execution), honestly labeled with the conditions it needed;
5. **working remote command execution** — attacker-controlled wire or
   request input makes a live target process on loopback execute a
   lab-chosen benign command, with an observed side effect and vulnerable,
   fixed and safe-input controls. Record the exact build, configuration,
   authentication, ASLR, grooming and triggering conditions; independent
   witness replay is required for ESTABLISHED. In-process harness markers,
   synthetic consumers and debugger-forced execution remain rung-4
   mechanics, not rung 5.

Unknowns stay UNKNOWN. Missing, failed or expired observations are never
reported as passes. Preserve failed hypotheses, negative results and

# mishe-tauftauf2shell — runtime2shell impact and RCE research plant

This repository is a Mishe plant with two general goals: **reaching rung 4
(demonstrated security impact) and, where a measured path exists, rung 5
(working remote command execution) for memory-safety vulnerabilities in
language runtimes and web-facing servers — the "X2Shell" family** — starting
with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) and Ruby2Shell
(CVE-2026-132825), and extending to similar classes the operator admits
under its standing mandate. Rung 5 is additive and per-build, never a reason
to relabel a pointer fault or harness-only marker as RCE. Everything here is
CC0. The durable products are the reproducible technical reports under
`reports/`; the laboratory under `lab/` is the means.

## Roles

- **one mind per target** (`ruby2shell`, `php2shell`, `node2shell`, and
  every target the operator admits) — each carries its own investigation:
  builds affected and patched runtimes, writes harnesses, instruments
  processes, runs debuggers, drives toward rung 4 and, where a measured
  path exists, rung 5 stage by stage, authors its report.
- **witness** — the independent verifier. Fresh context: re-runs claimed
  reproductions, hunts counterexamples, enforces the evidence ladder. The
  author's report is never acceptance.
- **operator** — the human owner's standing delegate with an expanded
  mandate: besides approving scoped work in place of the person, it holds
  the owner's standing approvals (recorded in the site's
  `operator/standing-approvals.md`) and actively **looks for similar
  things** — new X2Shell-class public claims, advisories and research
  worth a rung-4 or rung-5 attempt — proposing new targets with evidence,
  without asking each time. It is a mind, not a person; it never approves changes
  to this charter, systemd units or engine configuration, access to other
  plants or nodes, host-guard or credential changes, or anything off
  loopback.

One wake per role at a time; up to the site's `wake-concurrency.json` run
at once. Only the `omp` engine wakes minds here. No `claude`, no `codex`.

## Working in Mishe

A mind is a persistent identity (wall, intentions, history), not a
persistent process. You are woken for one turn by a trigger — an addressed
message, a changed signal, a due intention — and handed a dossier. Start
from it; the short `mishe` command resolves this site from
`$MISHE_SEED_HOME`, and an explicit `--home SITE_HOME` overrides it.
Resolve site-home paths to the absolute path before passing them to tools.

Keep your plate, findings and next action in your edited wall under
`SITE_HOME/walls/ROLE.md`, written for a human who has nothing else open:
what you are working on and why, the exact next command or edit, short
quoted evidence with where to look, and what would change your mind.
Update it while you work, not only at yield. Ask peers through addressed
messages on the shared chat tape. DMs are visible, not private.

Commit your own scoped work on the single `main` branch; a completed
checked change is committed, not parked. End every wake with
`mishe yield --result changed|verified|blocked`, your updated wall on
stdin; `--continue`, `--again DURATION` and `--when signal:NAME=VALUE`
schedule follow-up. A wake that ends without a yield is an unknown effect;
the next wake reconciles it first. While research is active, keep the chain
back-to-back: `--again 300`, never longer than the pin's cap; a genuine
wait for evidence is a `--when signal:` condition, not a long timer.

## Evidence discipline

Every finding carries evidence: the exact build, the exact input, the
observed bytes, and where they live. Distinguish, and never collapse:

1. **suspected vulnerability** — reasoning from source or claims, no trigger;
2. **reproducible crash** — a deterministic input that faults the lab process;
3. **confirmed memory corruption** — observed memory state proving
   corruption (ASan/UBSan/Valgrind report, debugger inspection), not just
   a crash;
4. **demonstrated security impact** — control exercised in the lab build
   (chosen bytes at chosen offsets; pointer control; benign marker

5. **working remote command execution** — attacker-controlled wire or

   authentication, ASLR, grooming and triggering conditions; independent
   witness replay is required for ESTABLISHED. In-process harness markers,
   synthetic consumers and debugger-forced execution remain rung-4
   mechanics, not rung 5.

# CVE-2026-135721 — FFmpeg: infinite loop in VC-2 RTP muxing

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135721 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/rtpenc_vc2hq.c::ff_rtp_send_vc2hq` |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`3b7147d`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-835 (Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition) |
| **Impact** | A Dirac/VC-2 data unit declaring a next parse offset of zero made the parsing pointer never advance, so the muxing loop ran forever. Crafted video remuxed to RTP could hang the process, consuming CPU indefinitely |
| **Vector** | attacker-supplied Dirac/VC-2 video remuxed to RTP |
| **Trigger** | data unit with `unit_size == 0` |

The vulnerable loop:

```c
// rtpenc_vc2hq.c — pre-fix (behavior in the lab)
while (unit < end) {
    unit_size = AV_RB32(&unit[5]);     // can be 0
    ...
    unit += unit_size;                 // never advances when 0
}
```

The fix bounds the loop and rejects short units:

```c
// fixed (commit 3b7147d, verbatim logic in the lab)
while (end - unit >= DIRAC_DATA_UNIT_HEADER_SIZE) {
    unit_size = AV_RB32(&unit[5]);
    if (unit_size < DIRAC_DATA_UNIT_HEADER_SIZE || unit_size > end - unit)
        break;
    ...
}
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The loop condition and unit-size validation did not guarantee forward progress.
A zero or undersized unit size left the pointer stationary. The fix requires a
full header of remaining bytes and rejects unit sizes below the header size.

## 2. Reproduction environment

| service | image | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vc2-vuln` | `cve-2026-135721:vuln` | non-advancing loop |
| `vc2-fixed` | `cve-2026-135721:fixed` | verbatim bounded loop |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-135721-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

The Python harness models the loop guards from both commits with a zero-size
unit, bounded to 1000 iterations to make the hang deterministic and observable.

./run-lab.sh up        # cve135721lab network: vc2-vuln / vc2-fixed
./run-lab.sh sweep
./run-lab.sh down
```

### V9.3

- Preserved scan defaults, filters, YARA-X pins, 512 MiB limit and background execution. PHP and Node remain separate scanners.

### V9.1

- Added compact startup, engine and unexpected-exit diagnostics for the new error property. Useful errors are kept separate from routine scan coverage gaps.
- Finished scans with only access, lock or file-size gaps can report FALSE when no vulnerable runtime was detected. Those skipped paths are listed separately; unassessable version/vendor evidence and limits that stop coverage still report UNKNOWN.
- Failed attempts preserve the previous completed results and scan log.
- Old workspaces, stale status/lock data and leftover launch markers no longer block a new scan. A live scan lock still prevents overlapping scans.
- Removed extra folder ownership/permission checks that could reject usable client folders; existing permissions are not changed.
- Temporary read locks on report files no longer stop a healthy scan; final report writes retry those locks.
- Unexpected worker exits without a completed current result now produce a useful scanner error, including long or wrapped PowerShell errors.
- Added common Configuration Manager/SCCM update-cache and distribution-point exclusions, plus precise Git object, browser/editor renderer, shader, Steam, Unreal derived-data, and Defender quarantine/history cache exclusions.

# Change notes

Changes for the PHP scanners covering **CVE-2026-109618** and **CVE-2026-109619**, grouped by operating system and version. Analysis changes are listed separately.

Current versions: Windows V7.1, Linux V7.3, Mac V7.1, and Results Analysis V7.2.

## Windows scanner

### V7.1

- Windows scans now tolerate temporary read locks on their status and error files instead of stopping unexpectedly.
- Improved early startup, engine and unexpected-exit reporting, including clearer Windows error messages. Failed attempts preserve the previous completed results and scan log.
- Old scan files, stale status/lock contents and leftover launch markers no longer block a new scan. A live scan lock still prevents overlapping scans.
- Removed extra folder ownership and permission checks that could reject usable client folders. Existing folder permissions are not changed.
- Added common Microsoft Configuration Manager/SCCM update-cache and distribution-point folder exclusions on Windows.
- Windows now skips additional Git object stores, browser/editor renderer caches, graphics shader caches, Steam caches, Unreal derived-data caches, and Defender quarantine/history folders. Application and per-user PHP locations remain eligible outside these excluded cache subtrees.
- Windows also skips these data/source file types: .dds, .pyi, .cmake, .def, .cs, .idl, .xaml and .parquet. Native libraries, extensionless files, final-extension matching and the PHP build-text exceptions are preserved. These scope exclusions apply to Quick, Normal and Deep.
- Reports UNKNOWN when PHP-version evidence may be incomplete at the 64-match capture limit. Confirmed vulnerable findings still take priority.

## Linux scanner

### V7.3

- Fixes a YARA-X startup crash reproduced on Ubuntu 18.04 when the client service has no HOME value. The scanner now supplies its own temporary configuration, without changing system libraries or the global environment, and does not load a user's personal YARA-X settings.
- Adds discovery inside mounted local SquashFS applications, including Snap mounts, after checking their backing storage is local.
- Adds OverlayFS discovery when all underlying layers can be verified as local. Remote filesystems remain excluded, including remote-backed SquashFS and OverlayFS mounts.
- Unverifiable backing storage is skipped with a coverage explanation and keeps the result UNKNOWN when no confirmed vulnerable PHP is found.
- Treats LXCFS as an intentionally excluded virtual system filesystem, avoiding an unsupported-filesystem warning for that exclusion.
- Uses one mount-information snapshot and applies existing directory exclusions before expensive backing-storage checks. Custom exclusions and valid alternate mount locations remain honored.
- Retains previous completed results on failure and removes the new temporary configuration and mount metadata with the scan workspace.
- Keeps the 512 MiB file limit, Normal defaults, two low-priority workers, existing PHP detection rules and Results Analysis V7.1 compatibility. Windows, Mac and the Analysis are unchanged.
- Passed 720 checks across 12 x64 Linux userlands and actual BigFix action tests on RHEL 8 and 9. New mount-selection tests used simulated metadata; real SquashFS/Overlay mounts and ARM64 were not newly tested for this release.

### V7.2

- Improved early startup, engine and unexpected-exit reporting. Failed attempts preserve the previous completed results and scan log.
- Old scan files, stale status/lock contents and leftover launch markers no longer block a new scan. A live scan lock still prevents overlapping scans.
- Removed extra folder ownership and permission checks that could reject usable client folders. Existing folder permissions are not changed.
- Settings with leading zeros are handled as decimal numbers. Bash 4.2 compatibility is retained, without requiring Python.

### V7.1

- Fixes scans stopping on RHEL 7.9 and CentOS 7.9 because of older Bash handling of empty option lists.
- Reports UNKNOWN when a file reaches the PHP version-match capture limit, preserving any confirmed vulnerable finding.
- Keeps the 512 MiB limit, scan presets, background operation and V7 Analysis compatibility.

# CVE-2026-135709 — FFmpeg: OOB write in OGG page buffering

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135709 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/oggenc.c::ogg_buffer_page` |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`f75923e`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write) |
| **Impact** | When the page-list allocation failed, `ogg_buffer_page()` returned without resetting the current page, which remained full. The next `ogg_buffer_data()` call then wrote into the stale full page with an invalid length, causing an out-of-bounds write |
| **Vector** | conditions that make page allocation fail during OGG muxing |
| **Trigger** | page-list allocation failure followed by a data write |

The vulnerable failure path:

```c
// oggenc.c — pre-fix (behavior in the lab)
OGGPageList *l = av_mallocz(sizeof(*l));
if (!l)
    return AVERROR(ENOMEM);   // current page left full/stale
```

The fix resets the page:

```c
// fixed (commit f75923e, verbatim in the lab)
if (!l) {
    ogg_reset_cur_page(oggstream);
    return AVERROR(ENOMEM);
}
```

---

## 1. Root cause

An error path returned without restoring the muxer's page state. The stale full
page was then reused by the data writer, which assumed room it did not have. The
fix resets the current page on allocation failure.

A mind is a persistent identity (wall, intentions, history), not a
persistent process. You are woken for one turn by a trigger — an addressed
message, a changed signal, a due intention — and handed a dossier. Start
from it; the short `mishe` command resolves this site from

Update it while you work, not only at yield. Ask peers through addressed

wait for evidence is a `--when signal:` condition, not a long timer.

## Evidence discipline

Every finding carries evidence: the exact build, the exact input, the
observed bytes, and where they live. Distinguish, and never collapse:

1. **suspected vulnerability** — reasoning from source or claims, no trigger;
2. **reproducible crash** — a deterministic input that faults the lab process;
3. **confirmed memory corruption** — observed memory state proving
   corruption (ASan/UBSan/Valgrind report, debugger inspection), not just
   a crash;
4. **demonstrated security impact** — control exercised in the lab build
   (chosen bytes at chosen offsets; pointer control; benign marker
   execution), honestly labeled with the conditions it needed;
5. **working remote command execution** — attacker-controlled wire or
   request input makes a live target process on loopback execute a
   lab-chosen benign command, with an observed side effect and vulnerable,
   fixed and safe-input controls. Record the exact build, configuration,
   authentication, ASLR, grooming and triggering conditions; independent
   witness replay is required for ESTABLISHED. In-process harness markers,
   synthetic consumers and debugger-forced execution remain rung-4
   mechanics, not rung 5.

Unknowns stay UNKNOWN. Missing, failed or expired observations are never

# `drupal-installer-scanner`

Detection-only triage for `CVE-2026-132165`, the `Drupal core` installer flaw (`SA-CORE-2026-017`) that lets an unauthenticated visitor try to reinstall a site that is already installed — and take it over. `Drupal` disclosed it on `18 Nov 2026`, rated it `Highly critical 20/25`, and later added that it was exploited on live sites as early as `19 Nov 2026 19:00 UTC`. `CISA` added it to its `Known Exploited Vulnerabilities` catalog on `24 Nov 2026`, due `27 Nov 2026`. Grades your core version against the fixed releases, reads the version your site already discloses, and probes `/core/install.php` with one plain `GET` to see whether the installer answers "already installed" or serves an install form. Nothing here sends a payload, submits a form, or `POST`s anything.

## `What it checks`

* `CVE-2026-132165` — `Drupal core` ships with `core/install.php`, and it stays on the site after installation. Under specific conditions, an anonymous visitor can use that installer to try to reinstall a finished site, which can lead to site takeover or remote code execution. `CVSS 3.1 9.8` (`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`) per `Tenable`, citing `Mitre`/`NVD`; a `CVSS 4.0` score of `9.2` is also in circulation, and `NVD` had not published a record of its own at the time of writing, so the `9.8` is the `Tenable` figure and the `9.2` is the second opinion — both agree it is critical, they disagree on the decimal. `CWE-94` (code injection) per the bulletin; some trackers also map it to `CWE-284` / `CWE-502`. Found by `Anthropic's OSS Scanner` (`ANT-2026-GMRPK0BU`).

Fixed versions, per the vendor advisory `SA-CORE-2026-017` (primary source):

| `Branch` | `Upgrade to` |
| --- | --- |
| `Drupal 10.6.x` | `10.6.22` (or later) |
| `Drupal 11.3.x` | `11.3.22` (or later) |
| `Drupal 11.4.x` | `11.4.13` (or later) |

`Drupal 11.2.x` and below, `10.5.x` and below, and `Drupal 8` and `9` are end of life and get no fix on those branches. `Drupal 11.5 beta` and `12.0` are listed as affected in the `16 November` PSA with no fixed release on those lines yet — this scanner grades them vulnerable and says so.

* The companion flaw, same releases, same fix. `CVE-2026-132166` (`SA-CORE-2026-018`, `Moderately critical 14/25`) is a gadget chain in `Drupal core` classes. It is not directly exploitable — it needs a separate bug that unserializes attacker input, and administrator access — so this scanner flags it in the same verdict rather than pretending it is a separate problem.

If you cannot update yet, block the installer. The advisory says to deny `/core/install.php` at the web server, with a prefix rule, not an exact-match rule — an exact-match rule lets `/core/install.php/foo` through. Keeping the web server from writing to or changing permissions on `settings.php` mitigates some, but not all, exploit paths.

## `Usage`

```bash
# grade a version string
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --version "11.4.12"
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --version "11.4.13"

# a live site: public reads only — CHANGELOG.txt, X-Generator, one GET of /core/install.php
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --url https://example.com

# the box that runs the site (web root or project root)
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --local-dir /var/www/html

# hunt the access logs for installer requests (POSTs are attack probes)
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --version "11.4.12" --access-log /var/log/nginx/access.log

# hunt a Drupal tree for PHP files under sites/*/files (uploaded shells)
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --version "11.4.12" --ioc-dir /var/www/html

# a whole fleet at once
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --inventory-json fleet.json

# machine output / the fixed-version table
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --version "11.4.12" --json

# CVE-2026-135212 — AiSOC: cross-tenant investigation run disclosure

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135212 |
| **Component** | AiSOC — `services/agents/app/api/investigate.py` |
| **Affected** | before 23.6.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`a52a55a`** (PR 1993) |
| **CWE** | CWE-639 (Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key) |
| **Impact** | Investigation routes looked up runs by `run_id` without checking that the run belonged to the caller's tenant. A signed-in user who learned another tenant's run id could read its audit logs, forensic output and incident reports through the GET route, report variants, the WebSocket stream, or agent-runs routes. The fix applies a tenant-scope guard on every route |
| **Vector** | authenticated user supplying another tenant's `run_id` |
| **Trigger** | known or guessed run id belonging to a different tenant |

The vulnerable lookup:

```python
# pre-fix (verbatim behavior in the lab)
run = get_run(run_id)     # keyed only by the caller-supplied id
if not run:
    ...
```

The fix checks tenant ownership:

```python
# fixed (commit a52a55a, verbatim in the lab)
if not run or str(run.get("tenant_id")) != str(scoped_tenant_or_403(principal)):
    ...
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The run id acted as a bearer capability without an authorization check tying it
to the caller's tenant. The fix validates `tenant_id` on every lookup, including
the streaming and report paths.

## 2. Reproduction environment

| service | image | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inv-vuln` | `cve-2026-135212:vuln` | run id alone grants access |
| `inv-fixed` | `cve-2026-135212:fixed` | verbatim tenant-scope guard |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-135212-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

The Python harness uses the guard from both commits with a victim-tenant run
requested by an attacker-tenant user. A legitimate same-tenant access is also
checked.

# CVE-2026-135089 — humhub/questions: missing access checks on answer actions

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135089 |
| **Component** | humhub/questions — `controllers/AnswerController.php` |
| **Affected** | through 1.1.5 |
| **Fixed in** | **`cdc3987`** (PR 55) |
| **CWE** | CWE-863 (Incorrect Authorization) |
| **Impact** | Answer edit, vote and select-best actions checked only the user's permission on the answer, not whether the parent question was published and non-archived. A user with answer-level rights could act on answers belonging to archived or unpublished questions. The fix adds visibility and `isAnswerable()` preconditions and HTML-encodes author names |
| **Vector** | authenticated user invoking an answer action on a protected question |
| **Trigger** | question not answerable (archived or unpublished) |

The vulnerable check:

```php
// pre-fix (verbatim behavior in the lab)
if (!$answer->canEdit()) { ... }        // no question-state check
```

The fix adds the precondition:

```php
// fixed (commit cdc3987, verbatim in the lab)
if (!$question->content->canView() || !$question->isAnswerable()
    || !$answer->canEdit()) { ... }
```

---

## 1. Root cause

Authorization was evaluated on the child answer in isolation. The state of the
owning question — whether it was published and open to answers — was ignored,
so actions remained available after a question was closed or archived. The fix
checks both the question and the answer.

## 2. Reproduction environment

| service | image | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hq-vuln` | `cve-2026-135089:vuln` | action without question precondition |
| `hq-fixed` | `cve-2026-135089:fixed` | verbatim precondition guard |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-135089-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

The Python harness uses the guard from both commits with an archived,
non-answerable question and a user who has edit rights on the answer. It also
checks a legitimate answerable question.

## 3. Running the environment

```sh
./run-lab.sh build     # builds both sides (python:3.12-alpine)
./run-lab.sh up        # cve135089lab network: hq-vuln / hq-fixed
./run-lab.sh sweep
./run-lab.sh down
```

## 4. The PoC

`poc/poc.py` (stdlib only):

* **check** — exit 1 when the action is allowed on a non-answerable question,
  0 when denied; 3 no worker, 2 unreachable.
* **exploit** — narrated c

# mishe-tauftauf2shell — runtime2shell impact and RCE research plant

This repository is a Mishe plant with two general goals: **reaching rung 4
(demonstrated security impact) and, where a measured path exists, rung 5
(working remote command execution) for memory-safety vulnerabilities in
language runtimes and web-facing servers — the "X2Shell" family** — starting
with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) and Ruby2Shell
(CVE-2026-132825), and extending to similar classes the operator admits
under its standing mandate. Rung 5 is additive and per-build, never a reason
to relabel a pointer fault or harness-only marker as RCE. Everything here is
CC0. The durable products are the reproducible technical reports under
`reports/`; the laboratory under `lab/` is the means.

## Roles

- **one mind per target** (`ruby2shell`, `php2shell`, `node2shell`, and
  every target the operator admits) — each carries its own investigation:
  builds affected and patched runtimes, writes harnesses, instruments
  processes, runs debuggers, drives toward rung 4 and, where a measured
  path exists, rung 5 stage by stage, authors its report.
- **witness** — the independent verifier. Fresh context: re-runs claimed
  reproductions, hunts counterexamples, enforces the evidence ladder. The
  author's report is never acceptance.
- **operator** — the human owner's standing delegate with an expanded
  mandate: besides approving scoped work in place of the person, it holds
  the owner's standing approvals (recorded in the site's
  `operator/standing-approvals.md`) and actively **looks for similar
  things** — new X2Shell-class public claims, advisories and research
  worth a rung-4 or rung-5 attempt — proposing new targets with evidence,
  without asking each time. It is a mind, not a person; it never approves changes
  to this charter, systemd units or engine configuration, access to other
  plants or nodes, host-guard or credential changes, or anything off
  loopback.

One wake per role at a time; up to the site's `wake-concurrency.json` run
at once. Only the `omp` engine wakes minds here. No `claude`, no `codex`.

## Working in Mishe

A mind is a persistent identity (wall, intentions, history), not a
persistent process. You are woken for one turn by a trigger — an addressed
message, a changed signal, a due intention — and handed a dossier. Start
from it; the short `mishe` command resolves this site from
`$MISHE_SEED_HOME`, and an explicit `--home SITE_HOME` overrides it.
Resolve site-home paths to the absolute path before passing them to tools.

Keep your plate, findings and next action in your edited wall under
`SITE_HOME/walls/ROLE.md`, written for a human who has nothing else open:
what you are working on and why, the exact next command or edit, short
quoted evidence with where to look, and what would change your mind.
Update it while you work, not only at yield. Ask peers through addressed
messages on the shared chat tape. DMs are visible, not private.

Commit your own scoped work on the single `main` branch; a completed
checked change is committed, not parked. End every wake with
`mishe yield --result changed|verified|blocked`, your updated wall on
stdin; `--continue`, `--again DURATION` and `--when signal:NAME=VALUE`
schedule follow-up. A wake that ends without a yield is an unknown effect;
the next wake reconciles it first. While research is active, keep the chain
back-to-back: `--again 300`, never longer than the pin's cap; a genuine
wait for evidence is a `--when signal:` condition, not a long timer.

## Evidence discipline

Every finding carries evidence: the exact build, the exact input, the
observed bytes, and where they live. Distinguish, and never collapse:

1. **suspected vulnerability** — reasoning from source or claims, no trigger;
2. **reproducible crash** — a deterministic input that faults the lab process;
3. **confirmed memory corruption** — observed memory state proving
   corruption (ASan/UBSan/Valgrind report, debugger inspection), not just
   a crash;
4. **demonstrated security impact** — control exercised in the lab build
   (chosen bytes at chosen offsets; pointer control; benign marker
   execution), honestly labeled with the conditions it needed;
5. **working remote command execution** — attacker-controlled wire or
   request input makes a live target process on loopback execute a
   lab-chosen benign command, with an observed side effect and vulnerable,
   fixed and safe-input controls. Record the exact build, configuration,
   authentication, ASLR, grooming and triggering conditions; independent
   witness replay is required for ESTABLISHED. In-process harness markers,
   synthetic consumers and debugger-forced execution remain rung-4
   mechanics, not rung 5.

Unknowns stay UNKNOWN. Missing, failed or expired observations are never
reported as passes. Preserve failed hypotheses, negative results and
contradictory evidence in the wall and the report;

# CVE-2026-123158 - OpenSSH Password Authentication Bypass (SSHole)

**CVE-2026-123158** | **CVSS 3.1: 8.1 (High)**

An authentication bypass in OpenSSH affecting Linux systems running musl libc without PAM.
SSHole is a password authentication bypass affecting OpenSSH's `sshd` implementation on Linux systems using musl libc without PAM.
The vulnerability originates from an interaction between OpenSSH's internal password verification logic and musl's `crypt()` implementation.
When a specially sized password is processed, musl's `crypt()` can return the literal string `*` instead of a valid password hash. OpenSSH does not correctly distinguish this error result from a legitimate stored password value.
For accounts whose shadow password field contains `*`, the comparison can consequently succeed.
An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this behaviour to bypass SSH password authentication and gain access to affected accounts.
The vulnerability is tracked as **CVE-2026-123158**.

## Affected Configurations

The vulnerability affects OpenSSH versions before 10.6p2 when running on Linux with musl libc and without PAM.

However, the authentication bypass requires additional account and configuration conditions.

The following conditions must be satisfied:

- OpenSSH is linked against musl libc.
- PAM is not used for SSH password authentication.
- `PasswordAuthentication` is enabled.
- At least one local account has a shadow password field containing exactly `*`.
- Another local account has a SHA-256 or SHA-512 password hash available for salt selection.
- The SSH service is reachable by the attacker.

For root authentication, `PermitRootLogin yes` must also be configured.

An account containing `!` in its shadow password field is not equivalent to an account containing `*` for this vulnerability.

### Potentially affected environments

- Alpine Linux systems running the non-PAM OpenSSH server.
- OpenWrt systems using affected musl-based OpenSSH builds.
- Buildroot-based Linux environments.
- Yocto-based embedded Linux distributions.
- Custom Linux images using musl libc and OpenSSH without PAM.

These platforms are not automatically vulnerable. Their OpenSSH build, authentication configuration and account database must satisfy the required conditions.

### Generally unaffected configurations

- OpenSSH using glibc rather than musl.
- OpenSSH configurations using PAM for password authentication.
- Systems with SSH password authentication disabled.
- Systems running a patched OpenSSH build.
- SSH implementations that do not use the affected OpenSSH authentication path.

## Technical Analysis

### 1. Password authentication

When PAM is disabled, OpenSSH performs password verification internally.

The authentication process involves the following operations:

1. The SSH client submits a password.
2. `sshd` retrieves the target account's stored password field.
3. OpenSSH determines which salt to use for password verification.
4. The supplied password is passed to `crypt()`.
5. The resulting value is compared against the stored password field.
6. Authentication succeeds or fails depending on the comparison.

The relevant implementation is found in:

```text
auth-passwd.c
openbsd-compat/xcrypt.c
openbsd-compat/port-uw.c
```

### 2. Salt selection

An important part of the vulnerability is how OpenSSH handles accounts without a usable password hash.

When the target account has a short password field, OpenSSH does not use that field directly as a cryptographic salt.

Instead, the compatibility implementation can select a salt from another local account containing a valid password hash.

The relevant function is:

```c
pick_salt()
```

This behaviour originated from earlier password-authentication timing protections, including work associated with CVE-2016-6210.

For SSHole, this salt-selection behaviour becomes part of the vulnerable execution path.

### 3. musl crypt() error handling

musl's SHA-256 and SHA-512 password hashing implementations impose a maximum password input length of 256 bytes.

When an input exceeds this limit, the hashing operation fails.

Instead of returning a valid password hash, musl's `crypt()` returns:

```text
*
```

This value is an error marker.

It is not a valid SHA-256 or SHA-512 password hash.

# CVE-2026-137084 — NodeBB: ActivityPub ingestion runs after the login redirect

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-137084 |
| **Component** | NodeBB — `Intents.create` controller |
| **Affected** | 4.12.0 before 4.16.4 |
| **Fixed in** | **`2f74bfa`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-698 (Execution After Redirect) |
| **Impact** | The unauthenticated branch called `helpers.redirect('/login')` but did not return, so execution fell through into the ActivityPub ingestion path. Unauthenticated attackers could send `GET /intents/create` with a remote note URI in `toPid` and inject federated content as local topics and posts |
| **Vector** | unauthenticated request to the intents endpoint |
| **Trigger** | redirect sent without a following return statement |

The old controller:

```js
// pre-fix (verbatim logic in the lab)
if (!authenticated) {
    helpers.redirect(res, '/login');   // no return; execution continues
}
// ingestion path runs for everyone
```

The fix adds the missing return:

```js
// fixed (commit 2f74bfa, verbatim in the lab)
if (!authenticated) {
    return helpers.redirect(res, '/login');
}
```

## 1. Root cause

A redirect response was emitted but control flow was not stopped. Code after
the branch assumed the caller was authorized because the redirect looked like a
guard. The fix makes the redirect terminal.

## 2. Reproduction environment

| service | image | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nbb-vuln` | `cve-2026-137084:vuln` | execution continues after redirect |
| `nbb-fixed` | `cve-2026-137084:fixed` | verbatim return guard |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-137084-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

Both sides are Python 3.12 images. The harness copies the controller flow from
the two commits. An unauthenticated `toPid` request is sent; an authenticated
flow is also checked.

## 3. Running the environment

```sh
./run-lab.sh build
./run-lab.sh up
./run-lab.sh sweep
./run-lab.sh down
```

The lab uses the isolated `cve137084lab` network and bounded containers.

## 4. The PoC

`poc/poc.py` takes a mode and an optional `--host=...`:

| mode | result |
| --- | --- |
| `check` | exit 1 when ingestion runs after the redirect, 0 when the return stops it |
| `exploit` | runs the full chain and reports the injected note |
| `probe` | prints the execution flag |
| `mitigation` | checks the return guard |

A standalone exploit ships at `exploit/exploit.py`:

```sh
python3 exploit/exploit.py --host=nbb-vuln
```

# CVE-2026-131827 — RustDesk: local privilege escalation through unvalidated registry recovery

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-131827 |
| **Component** | RustDesk Client for Windows — registry recovery |
| **Affected** | affected Windows builds before the fix |
| **Fixed in** | **PR 17040** |
| **CWE** | CWE-862 (Missing Authorization) |
| **Impact** | The registry recovery path applied pending registry state without checking the current value's type or length. A local attacker who could run low-privileged code could plant a mismatched pending value and steer the privileged recovery write, escalating to the service's privileges |
| **Vector** | local attacker modifying pending registry state |
| **Trigger** | recovery write with a mismatched value type or length |

The old recovery:

```rust
// pre-fix (verbatim logic in the lab)
// pending value applied without validation
```

The fix compares before writing:

```rust
// fixed (PR 17040, verbatim logic in the lab)
if cur_reg_value.vtype != reg_recovery.old.1
    || cur_reg_value.bytes.len() != reg_recovery.old.0.len() {
    // reject the recovery
}
```

## 1. Root cause

Recovery restored state it never re-validated. A tampered pending value was
written with elevated rights. The fix pins the write to the value shape that
was actually pending.

## 2. Reproduction environment

| service | image | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rd-vuln` | `cve-2026-131827:vuln` | pending value applied |
| `rd-fixed` | `cve-2026-131827:fixed` | verbatim shape guard |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-131827-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

Both sides are Python 3.12 images. The harness copies the validation from the
two commits. A mismatched pending value is applied; a matching one is also
checked.

## 3. Running the environment

```sh
./run-lab.sh build
./run-lab.sh up
./run-lab.sh sweep
./run-lab.sh down
```

The lab uses the isolated `cve131827lab` network and bounded containers.

## 4. The PoC

`poc/poc.py` takes a mode and an optional `--host=...`:

| mode | result |
| --- | --- |
| `check` | exit 1 when a mismatched value is applied, 0 when rejected |
| `exploit` | runs the full chain and reports the elevated write |
| `probe` | prints the elevation flag |
| `mitigation` | checks the shape guard |

A standalone exploit ships at `exploit/exploit.py`:

```sh
python3 exploit/exploit.py --host=rd-vuln
```

It exits 1 on a confirmed elevation and 0 on a safe target.

# CVE-2026-136950 — Ghostty: OSC 8 hyperlink injection on macOS

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-136950 |
| **Component** | Ghostty — macOS OSC 8 hyperlink handler |
| **Affected** | through 1.3.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`54fe8e1`** / v1.4.0 |
| **CWE** | CWE-74 (Injection) |
| **Impact** | OSC 8 hyperlinks from terminal output were opened with the trusted URL policy. A remote attacker able to emit a crafted escape sequence, for example through manipulated log output, could open dangerous URL schemes without confirmation. The fix routes OSC 8 URLs through `openUntrustedURL()` with a scheme allowlist and confirmation flow |
| **Vector** | malicious OSC 8 escape sequence in terminal output |
| **Trigger** | OSC 8 link with a dangerous URL scheme |

The old handler:

```swift
// pre-fix (verbatim logic in the lab)
// OSC 8 URL opened with the trusted policy, no scheme check
```

The fix:

```swift
// fixed (commit 54fe8e1, verbatim logic in the lab)
if action.kind == .osc8 {
    return openUntrustedURL(action.url)
}
private static func openUntrustedURL(_ value: String) -> Bool {
    let target = UntrustedURL(value)
    // allow / confirm / block by scheme
}
```

## 1. Root cause

Terminal output is untrusted data, but the hyperlink handler treated its URLs as
trusted. That let an attacker-controlled escape sequence invoke the same opening
path as a user-initiated link. The fix applies an untrusted-URL policy to OSC 8
actions.

## 2. Reproduction environment

| service | image | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ght-vuln` | `cve-2026-136950:vuln` | dangerous scheme opened |
| `ght-fixed` | `cve-2026-136950:fixed` | verbatim untrusted policy |
| `poc` | `cve-2026-136950-poc:local` | stdlib-only Python driver |

Both sides are Python 3.12 images. The harness copies the URL policy from the
two commits. A `file://` link is submitted; a normal `https://` link is also
checked.

## 3. Running the environment

```sh
./run-lab.sh build
./run-lab.sh up
./run-lab.sh sweep
./run-lab.sh down
```

The lab uses the isolated `cve136950lab` network and bounded containers.

## 4. The PoC

`poc/poc.py` takes a mode and an optional `--host=...`:

| mode | result |
| --- | --- |
| `check` | exit 1 when a dangerous URL is opened, 0 when blocked |
| `exploit` | runs the full chain and reports the unsafe open |
| `probe` | prints the unsafe-open flag |
| `mitigation` | checks the untrusted-URL policy |

A standalone exploit ships at `exploit/exploit.py`:

```sh
python3 exploit/exploit.py --host=ght-vuln
```

| **Affected** | before 1.2.0 |
| **Fixed in** | **`ee00464`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-918 (Server-Side Request Forgery) |
| **Impact** | String-based URL validation could be bypassed with DNS names, bracketed IPv6 literals and IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses. An attacker using prompt injection to influence a URL passed to the webpage-to-markdown or git-repo-to-markdown tool could fetch loopback services, internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints |
| **Vector** | prompt-injected URL passed to a markdownify tool |
| **Trigger** | URL resolving to a private, loopback or IPv4-mapped IPv6 address |

The old validation:

```ts
// pre-fix (verbatim logic in the lab)
// string prefix checks on the host; resolved address never checked
```

The fix validates the resolved address:

```ts
// fixed (commit ee00464, verbatim logic in the lab)
// reject private, loopback and IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses before fetching
```

## 1. Root cause

The validator worked on the URL string, not the address the resolver would
connect to. Encodings such as `::ffff:127.0.0.1` passed the string checks while
resolving to loopback. The fix resolves and validates the address.

Both sides are Python 3.12 images. The harness copies the validation decision
from the two commits. An IPv4-mapped loopback URL is submitted; a public IP is
also checked.
